name: Canaanites
also_known_as: Phoenicians (the coastal Canaanites of later times)
summary: The Bronze Age inhabitants of the land God promised to Abraham — a patchwork of city-states between the Jordan and the Mediterranean, worshipping Baal and Asherah. 'Canaanite' is both the name of one people and the umbrella term for all the nations of the land. Their descendants are part of the Levantine population today.
name_meaning: Canaan (Kena'an) is of uncertain meaning. It may mean 'lowland', or it may come from a word for purple dye, the region's famous export; 'Canaanite' also came to mean 'merchant'.

origin.account: Canaan was the fourth son of Ham, son of Noah. After Ham saw his father's nakedness, Noah cursed Canaan to be a servant to his brethren. Canaan's sons became Sidon, Heth and the Jebusite, Amorite, Girgasite, Hivite, Arkite, Sinite, Arvadite, Zemarite and Hamathite peoples, 'and afterward were the families of the Canaanites spread abroad' from Sidon to Gaza and the Dead Sea cities.

lineage.notes: Genesis 10 treats the Hittites, Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites and Hivites as Canaan's children, alongside Sidon (the Phoenicians). The recurring list of 'seven nations' adds the Perizzites and the Canaanites proper — the lowland and coastal population.

homeland.region: Canaan — from Sidon to Gaza and the Dead Sea
homeland.description: The land west of the Jordan, stretching north to the Lebanon coast. Scripture calls it 'a land flowing with milk and honey'. The Canaanites proper lived especially 'by the sea, and by the coast of Jordan' — the plains and valleys where chariots could operate — while other groups held the hills.
homeland.modern_location: Israel, the Palestinian territories, Lebanon, and western Syria and Jordan.

places.name: Hazor
places.note: 'The head of all those kingdoms'; burned by Joshua, later ruled by Jabin king of Canaan.

places.name: Megiddo
places.note: Canaanite city the tribes did not at first capture.

places.name: Jericho
places.note: First city taken in the conquest; Rahab's home.

places.name: Gezer
places.note: Remained Canaanite until Pharaoh gave it to Solomon.

places.name: Ugarit
places.note: Northern city whose tablets preserve Canaanite myths of Baal, El and Asherah (not named in the Bible).

timeline.event: Abram arrives at Shechem — 'and the Canaanite was then in the land' — and God promises the land to his seed.
Abraham buries Sarah in a field bought from Hittites; Judah marries a Canaanite and fathers Shelah and, through Tamar, Pharez.
Rulers of Canaanite city-states write to Pharaoh in the Amarna letters, complaining of unrest and of the 'Habiru'.
Israel enters Canaan; Jericho, Ai and Hazor fall, but many Canaanites remain in the plains and cities.
Jabin king of Canaan, with 900 iron chariots under Sisera, oppresses Israel twenty years; Deborah and Barak defeat him.
Solomon puts the surviving Canaanite populations to forced labour.
Coastal Canaanites continue as the Phoenicians of Tyre and Sidon; inland Canaanites merge with Israel.
A Canaanite woman from the region of Tyre and Sidon begs Jesus to heal her daughter; he praises her great faith.

religion.practices: Fertility worship at high places, with standing pillars and Asherah poles. It involved cult prostitution and, at its extreme, child sacrifice. Israel was warned not to learn 'the abominations of those nations', and the prophets called the later Baal worship in Israel the root of its downfall.

importance: Canaan is the stage of the Old Testament and the substance of God's land promise to Abraham. God delayed giving the land for four hundred years because 'the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full'. The conquest is presented as judgement on persistent evil, not favouritism: Israel is told it was not given the land for its own righteousness, and would be expelled for the same sins. Canaanites like Rahab who turned to God were spared and even entered the Messiah's line. Canaanite religion was also Israel's great temptation for centuries.

impact.how: Lived as sojourners among the Canaanites, owning only a burial field.
A Canaanite of Jericho who hid the spies, was saved with her household, and became mother of Boaz.
Judah's Canaanite marriage and his dealings with Tamar produced the line of Pharez, ancestor of David.
Baal worship drew Israel away repeatedly, most dramatically under Ahab and Jezebel.
Her persistent faith won healing for her daughter and became a sign of the gospel to the Gentiles.

notable_people.role: Priest-king of Salem, who blessed Abram (his people are not named)

key_verses.text: And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh. And the Canaanite was then in the land.
But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.

Not for thy righteousness, or for the uprightness of thine heart, dost thou go to possess their land: but for the wickedness of these nations the LORD thy God doth drive them out from before thee, and that he may perform the word which the LORD sware unto thy fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.
Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.

fate.summary: The Canaanites were not wiped out. Those who remained lived among Israel, were put to forced labour, intermarried and were absorbed over the centuries. On the coast they continued as the Phoenicians, whose colony Carthage in North Africa still called its people 'Chanani' in Augustine's day (5th century AD).

today.summary: Ancient DNA has shown that Canaanite ancestry never vanished. A 2017 study sequencing Bronze Age Canaanites from Sidon found that present-day Lebanese derive most of their ancestry (about 93%) from a Canaanite-related population. Other Levantine peoples — Jews, Palestinians, Jordanians, Syrians — also carry substantial Canaanite-related ancestry.
today.descendants: Modern Levantine populations, especially the Lebanese.
today.modern_legacy: The alphabet developed among Canaanite scribes (via Phoenician) and is the ancestor of Hebrew, Greek, Latin and Arabic scripts. Hebrew itself is a Canaanite language — Isaiah calls it 'the language of Canaan'.

archaeology.name: Amarna letters
archaeology.location: British Museum, Vorderasiatisches Museum Berlin, Egyptian Museum Cairo and others
archaeology.significance: Diplomatic tablets from Canaanite kings of Jerusalem, Shechem, Gezer, Megiddo and elsewhere to the Pharaoh — a snapshot of Canaan before Israel.

archaeology.name: Ugarit (Ras Shamra) tablets
archaeology.significance: The Baal Cycle and other myths explain the gods the Bible opposes: El, Baal, Asherah, Anat and Mot.

archaeology.name: Hazor destruction layer
archaeology.significance: A massive fire destroyed the Canaanite palace, with Canaanite statues deliberately smashed; the excavators connect it to Joshua 11.
